background_notes.fact: For the chosen compact C⊆Space and Ktime=[3t0/4,5t0/4], Kprod=C×Ktime is compact and is contained in the open set U. The C∞ real field d on U is continuous on Kprod.

Provides C∞ regularity of d on U.
Space has its finite real product topology.
U is exactly the positive-time domain.
t0>0 and the displayed inequalities put Ktime inside I⊆(0,∞).

background_notes.justification: Closed bounded intervals in ℝ are compact, and a product of two compact spaces is compact (the finite-product open-cover theorem). This includes empty C. The time projection makes U open. Smoothness implies relative continuity on U, and restricting a continuous map to a subset preserves continuity, giving the claimed ContinuousOn statement.

background_notes.fact: Every compact C⊆Space=Fin n→ℝ is Borel measurable and has finite dx-measure for the product Lebesgue measure of D014, including n=0.

grounds.reason: Space is a finite product of real lines with its Borel structure.
dx is exactly the product of standard real Lebesgue measures.

background_notes.justification: A finite product of real lines is Hausdorff, so compact C is closed and therefore Borel. Each coordinate projection of C is compact in ℝ and bounded. Since there are finitely many coordinates, choose a real R≥1 bounding all coordinates; if C is empty the inclusion is automatic. Then C lies in the closed box ∏j[-R,R]. Its product Lebesgue measure is the finite product (2R)^n, and measure monotonicity gives dx(C)≤(2R)^n<∞. For n=0 the box is the singleton empty tuple and the empty product is 1.

background_notes.fact: For every positive r the scalar sections x↦e(x,r) and x↦d(x,r) are continuous on Space and are dx-ae strongly measurable. In particular e(·,r) is ae strongly measurable eventually as r→t0, and d(·,t0) is ae strongly measurable.

grounds.reason: e and d are C∞ on the open positive-time domain U.
Space carries its product topology and Borel measurable structure.
For r>0 the whole section x↦(x,r) lies in U.
dx is a measure on this Borel space.
stime is an open neighborhood of t0 contained in the positive half-line.

background_notes.justification: Composing the continuous section x↦(x,r) with a smooth, hence continuous, field on U gives a continuous real function. A continuous real function on a Borel space is Borel measurable, and real-valued Borel measurable functions are strongly measurable because ℝ is separable; explicitly they admit pointwise simple approximations by truncation and dyadic rounding. Strong measurability implies ae strong measurability for dx. Since every r in the neighborhood stime is positive, the eventual assertion follows.
